title: The 'My Brain Doesn't Write' Reframe Script Bank
howToUse: This is your ready-to-use reframe script bank — seventeen self-coaching prompts and perspective-shift scripts, each written for a specific stuck moment you'll hit as you write your own copy inside this programme. When the blank page lands, when you're on your twelfth rewrite, or when the post-publish spiral starts: open this document, find the moment that matches, read the script out loud or into your notes, and keep moving. You do not need to memorise anything. You use the scripts exactly as written.
promise: These seventeen scripts redirect the fear that your brain isn't wired to write — so you can move from stuck to moving in under two minutes at any point in your copy process.

tools.name: Scripts 1–6: The Blank Page Stuck Moment
tools.instructions: Open this section the moment you start a new document and feel nothing come out — read the script that matches where you are, say it once, then write your next sentence.
tools.content:
These six scripts are for the moment before a single word exists on the page. Each one is a complete self-coaching turn you deliver to yourself.

---

"The discomfort I feel right now is not a signal that I can't do this. It's the same feeling I have in the first three minutes of every discovery call — before I settle in and start actually hearing the person. I'm going to write one sentence and stay in the room."

tools.content:
These six scripts are for the moment before a single word exists on the page. Each one is a complete self-coaching turn you deliver to yourself.

---

**Script 1 — When you open the document and immediately want to close it**

"The discomfort I feel right now is not a signal that I can't do this. It's the same feeling I have in the first three minutes of every discovery call — before I settle in and start actually hearing the person. I'm going to write one sentence and stay in the room."

---

**Script 2 — When you think 'I don't even know where to start'**

"I don't need to know where to start. I need to know what I would say first if a client I loved messaged me right now asking what this offer actually does. I'm going to write that — nothing else, just that."

---

**Script 3 — When you feel like everything you write sounds wrong before you've written it**

"I'm editing before I'm drafting. Those are two different jobs and I've accidentally assigned them both to the same moment. My only job right now is to get something on the page. Wrong words on a page are infinitely more useful than the right words still in my head."

---

**Script 4 — When you think 'I need to do more research before I can write'**

"Research is a legitimate task and it is also my favourite way to avoid writing. I already know this client. I have spoken to them for hundreds of hours. I am going to write from what I already know and flag any gaps to check later — in square brackets, in the draft itself."

---

**Script 5 — When the page feels too high-stakes to start**

"This draft is not the sales page. This draft is the conversation I need to have with myself about the sales page before I write the sales page. Nothing I write in the next twenty minutes is going public. I'm just thinking out loud in a document."

---

**Script 6 — When you can't choose between two directions and that's stopping you from starting either**

"I'm treating this like a decision I have to get right before I move. It isn't. I'm going to pick one direction, write 150 words in it, and see which one sounds like me when I read it back. The right one will be obvious once I can see both."

---

tools.name: Scripts 7–12: The Rewrite Spiral Stuck Moment
tools.instructions: Use this section when you've been rewriting the same sentence, paragraph, or headline for more than ten minutes — read the matching script, then follow the one instruction at the e
tools.content:
These six scripts are for the middle of the writing process — when you're not blank anymore, but you've locked onto one section and can't leave it.

---

**Script 7 — When you've rewritten the same sentence twelve times and it still feels wrong**

"I've stopped trying to write and started trying to perform. The sentence isn't broken — I am trying to make it do something it was never meant to do by itself. I'm going to move to the next sentence and come back to this one when the rest of the paragraph exists around it."

---

**Script 8 — When you feel like a 'real' copywriter would have nailed this on the first try**

"The copywriters I am comparing myself to are showing me their fourth draft, not their first. Every piece of copy I have ever admired was rewritten. The question isn't whether this needs more work — it's whether I'm rewriting it or just rereading it with increasing anxiety. Right now it's the second one. I'm moving on."

---

**Script 9 — When the headline section has eaten forty-five minutes and you haven't touched the body copy**

"A headline I can't get right is usually a sign I haven't decided what the single most important thing this offer does actually is. That's a clarity problem, not a writing problem. I'm going to skip the headline, write the body copy as if the headline already exists, and come back. The right headline almost always appears inside the body copy."

---

**Script 10 — When everything you write sounds like someone else's copy and not yours**

"I sound like someone else because I have read too much copy this week and not enough of my own words. I'm going to open my last voice note, or the last email a client sent me that I really loved, or a message I wrote when I wasn't thinking about copy at all — and I'm going to read that first. That's the register I'm writing in."

---

**Script 11 — When you think 'this is too simple, it can't be right'**

"Simple is not the same as shallow. The clearest thing I have ever said to a client on a call was also the simplest — and it was the sentence they quoted back to me three months later. Simple means I have actually understood something well enough to say it plainly. That is not a failure of sophistication. That is the work."

---

**Script 12 — When you feel the urge to start a completely different section because this one feels stuck**

"Jumping sections is fine if I've genuinely extracted everything I have on this one. It is not fine if I'm running away from the hard question this section is asking me. The hard question this section is asking me right now is: [WRITE THE QUESTION IN YOUR OWN WORDS]. I'll answer that question in one sentence before I move."

---

tools.name: Scripts 13–17: The Post-Publish Spiral Stuck Moment
tools.instructions: Use this section in the hours or days after you hit send or publish — when the second-guessing starts; read the script that matches the thought you're having and say it before you
tools.content:
These five scripts are for after the copy goes out — the moment when everything that felt decided suddenly doesn't.

---

**Script 13 — When you hit send and immediately want to recall it**

"The discomfort I feel right now is not evidence that the email was wrong. It is evidence that I care about my work and my readers, which is exactly the quality that makes my copy worth reading in the first place. I'm going to close the sent folder and not reread it for at least two hours."

---

**Script 14 — When open rates come in lower than you hoped and you decide the copy was the problem**

"Open rates are a subject line and a send-time measurement. They tell me almost nothing about the quality of what was inside. Before I rewrite anything, I need to know what the click rate was — because that's the copy's actual scorecard. I'm going to look at the full data before I change a single word."

---

**Script 15 — When no one replies and you interpret that as 'no one connected with it'**

"The people who connected with this most are the ones least likely to reply. They are quietly deciding. The silence after a good email looks identical to the silence after a bad one, and I have no way to tell the difference until the booking comes in or the next email lands. I'm going to send the next one."

---

**Script 16 — When you compare your copy to another coach's page and yours feels embarrassing by comparison**

"I am comparing my first ten attempts to someone else's hundredth. I also have no idea whether their copy is converting — I only know that it looks polished. My copy is in my voice, about my methodology, written by the person who actually understands what transformation happens inside this container. That is an advantage no hired copywriter can give them and I am only at the start of learning to use it."

---

**Script 17 — When you think 'I should have just hired someone' after publishing something you're not proud of**

"The copy I'm not proud of is the tuition for the copy I will be proud of. Every coach I know who now writes with confidence went through a version of this exact moment — and the only difference between them and the coaches who never got there is that they sent the next email anyway. I'm writing the next one. Not the perfect one. The next one."

---

**A note on using all seventeen scripts together:**

You do not need to read through all seventeen before you start. The moment you notice you've stopped moving — blank page, rewrite spiral, post-publish dread — match your feeling to the section heading and go straight there. Each script is designed to produce one physical action: the next sentence, the next section, or the next send. That is the only outcome any of them is trying to create.

nextStep.heading: Where This Goes Inside the Programme
nextStep.body: The scripts in this bank are most useful at the exact moments the programme's core training predicts: when you've finished a module on the Client Psychology Reverse-Map and opened a new document to apply it to your actual sales page, and everything you understood thirty minutes ago has evaporated. That is normal, it is the gap the programme is built to close, and it is exactly when Scripts 1–6 belong in front of you. Keep this document open alongside every writing session you do inside the programme — not as reading material, but as a tool you reach for when you stop moving. Your first live writing task is the sales page diagnosis exercise. Open it now.
